title: Süleymaniye Mosque & Historic Bazaar Quarter: Quiet Ottoman Masterpiece
seoTitle: Süleymaniye Mosque Istanbul: Views, Tombs & Visiting Guide
metaDescription: Plan a calm visit to Süleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul: prayer times, Suleiman and Hürrem's tombs, Golden Horn views, and nearby kuru fasulye spots.
quickAnswer: Built by Mimar Sinan between 1550 and 1557 on Istanbul's Third Hill, Süleymaniye Mosque offers free daily entry outside prayer times, panoramic Golden Horn views, and far thinner crowds than Sultanahmet. Pair the mosque with the garden tombs of Sultan Suleiman and Hürrem Sultan, then cross the street for a classic kuru fasulye lunch.

body.text: Why is Süleymaniye quieter and grander than the Blue Mosque?

Süleymaniye Mosque feels quieter and grander than the Blue Mosque because it sits uphill from the main tour-bus drop-off loop and spans a vast imperial complex designed by Mimar Sinan. Inside, natural light pours through restrained stained glass onto pale stonework, creating calm acoustics and monumental scale without the long queues common in Sultanahmet.

Tour coaches rarely climb the narrow streets leading up from Eminönü and the Grand Bazaar, which naturally filters foot traffic. Instead of herding past ropes in a crowded prayer hall, visitors can walk freely across the marble courtyard, study the four minarets with ten balconies—symbolizing Suleiman as the fourth Ottoman sultan in Istanbul and tenth in the dynasty—and pause under a 53-meter central dome engineered for clarity of sound. As part of the [UNESCO Historic Areas of Istanbul](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/356/), the surrounding külliye (complex) once housed madrasas, a hospital, a soup kitchen, and a hamam, giving the hilltop a neighborhood rhythm rather than a theme-park feel.

body.text: What views and tombs (Suleiman & Hürrem) sit inside the complex?

The rear garden of Süleymaniye holds the octagonal mausoleums of Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent and his wife Hürrem Sultan, set amid weathered Ottoman gravestones. Just beyond the garden wall, a long stone terrace opens onto an unobstructed panorama across the Golden Horn, Galata Tower, the Bosphorus entrance, and the Asian shore.

Step through the garden gate behind the qibla wall to visit both tombs at a slow pace. Suleiman's mausoleum features a double dome, deep-blue and coral-red İznik tiles, and a carved stone canopy, while Hürrem Sultan's smaller neighboring tomb displays delicate floral ceramic panels from the peak of sixteenth-century İznik workshops ([Istanbul Tour Studio](https://istanbultourstudio.com/things-to-do/suleymaniye-mosque)). Before leaving the hilltop, walk two minutes past the northern corner of the complex to Mimar Sinan's modest triangular tomb—a quiet final statement from the empire's chief architect. Morning light favors photos toward the Bosphorus, while late afternoon casts warm gold across Galata and Karaköy.

Süleymaniye Mosque is open daily to non-worshipping visitors roughly from 08:30 to 18:45, except during the five daily Islamic prayers when the main hall closes for about 30 minutes. On Fridays, tourist entry pauses longer around midday—typically from 12:00 to 13:30—for congregational prayer, and modest dress is mandatory ([Süleymaniye Opening Hours Guide](https://www.tickets-istanbul.com/suleymaniye-mosque/opening-hours-prayer-times/)).
Because prayer schedules shift by several minutes every week with the sun, check the day's ezan times before climbing the hill. Use this practical checklist before entering:

items: Cover shoulders and knees: Both men and women need long trousers or skirts; women must wear a headscarf (free loaner scarves and wraps are available at the visitor entrance).
Remove shoes cleanly: Take off footwear before stepping onto the carpeted hall and carry shoes in the provided plastic bags.
Keep voices low and flash off: Worshippers pray quietly throughout the day, so avoid tripod setups and loud commentary inside.
Time your terrace stop: If you arrive during a 30-minute prayer closure, spend that window on the Golden Horn viewpoint terrace or browsing the outer courtyard.

body.text: Where do you eat classic kuru fasulye nearby?

Directly across Prof. Dr. Sıddık Sami Onar Caddesi from the mosque's main gate sits Istanbul's most famous strip for kuru fasulye—slow-simmered white haricot beans served over buttered rice pilav with mixed pickles and raw onion. Long-running houses like Erzincanlı Ali Baba and Kanaat Lokantası serve fast, affordable lunches to students, merchants, and travelers.

Most kitchens along this row cook Erzincan or Çayeli-style white beans in rich tomato-and-butter sauces, sometimes with tender chunks of beef or pastırma. [Kurufasülyeci Erzincanlı Ali Baba](https://mekan.com/mekan/suleymaniyeli-kurufasulyeci-erzincanli-ali-baba) at No. 7 and neighboring [Ali Baba Kanaat Lokantası](https://mekan.com/mekan/kurufasulyeci-kanaat-lokantasi) turn tables quickly between 11:30 and 14:30; arrive before noon or after 14:00 for a relaxed window seat. Pair your plate with cold ayran or Cacık, and save room for sütlaç (baked rice pudding) before strolling downhill through the historic bazaar quarter toward Eminönü.

faq.q: Is there an entrance fee for Süleymaniye Mosque in 2026?
faq.a: No. Entry to Süleymaniye Mosque, its courtyard, and the garden tombs of Suleiman and Hürrem Sultan is free. Voluntary donations are accepted at the exit box.

faq.q: How do I reach Süleymaniye Mosque by public transit?
faq.a: Take the T1 tram to Beyazıt–Kapalıçarşı or Laleli–Üniversite and walk 10 to 12 minutes north past Istanbul University, or take the M2 metro to Vezneciler and walk 10 minutes uphill.

faq.q: Are the tombs of Suleiman and Hürrem open at the same hours as the mosque?
faq.a: The tombs generally open around 09:00 and close earlier than the main prayer hall, usually between 16:30 and 17:30. Visit the garden tombs before late afternoon.

faq.q: Can I walk from Süleymaniye Mosque to the Grand Bazaar and Spice Bazaar?
faq.a: Yes. Both bazaars lie roughly 10 to 12 minutes downhill on foot through the historic merchant streets of Tahtakale and Mercan.

faq.q: Do I need to bring my own headscarf to Süleymaniye Mosque?
faq.a: Bringing a lightweight scarf is convenient, though the visitor entrance lends clean headscarves and long skirts free of charge.

faq.q: What is the best time of day to photograph the Golden Horn from Süleymaniye?
faq.a: Between 09:00 and 10:30 for clear light over the Bosphorus and Galata, or roughly one hour before sunset when the water turns warm gold.
